label: Person
name: Adolphus XIII of Holstein
summary:
Adolphus XIII of Holstein-Schauenburg (c. 1524–1576) was the last Count of Holstein-Schauenburg, presiding over the extinction of his dynasty's independent comital line. A member of the Holstein-Schauenburg house that had governed the Schauenburg and Holstein territories since the twelfth century, Adolphus XIII ruled in the era of the Protestant Reformation's consolidation in northern Germany, when the region's small dynasties were navigating the religious and political upheavals that accompanied the Reformation's spread.

The Holstein-Schauenburg dynasty's extinction with Adolphus XIII represents the typical pattern of many smaller German dynasties in the Reformation era — the combination of dynastic failure (lack of male heirs), religious change, and the consolidation of larger territorial states absorbed many formerly independent counties. The Holstein territories passed to Denmark after the dynasty's extinction, while Schauenburg's fate involved complex negotiations among neighbouring powers.

Adolphus XIII's reign thus marks the end of a dynasty whose roots went back to the high medieval period. His name — reflecting the long tradition of 'Adolph' as a Holstein-Schauenburg dynastic name, a tradition going back to the famous Count Adolf II of Holstein who colonised the Slavic east — represents the accumulated prestige of a house that had shaped northern German history for four centuries before its extinction.
